question: True or false: one gene largely decides whether a person finds the chemical PTC bitter?
answer: True. Variants of a single bitter-receptor gene, TAS2R38, explain most of the difference, by one estimate 55% to 85% of it. The trait surfaced by accident in 1931, when the chemist Arthur Fox spilled PTC powder at DuPont: a colleague complained of the bitterness while Fox, closer to it, tasted nothing.
move: Before explaining a difference in general terms, look for a single switch.
trap: Assuming a taste trait, like most traits, spreads across hundreds of genes.
reference: Kim, Jorgenson, Coon, Leppert, Risch & Drayna, Positional cloning of the human quantitative trait locus underlying taste sensitivity to phenylthiocarbamide, Science, 2003
